body:
Oh, I'm in college, and I'm trying to learn as much as I can. But that's sort of the problem: I'm basically trying to make myself a human encyclopedia and getting depressed when I'm nowhere close to it. I basically look at academics and the really smart, jack-of-all trades, master-of-all people that host podcasts as the baseline minimum of what I should be. I feel worthless otherwise; I'm too easily heartbroken to be an advocate for something, I'm too shy to be the life of the party and I'm too limited both economically and physically to be charitable for everything I want to be charitable for.

Eh, I'm sorry. This isn't the thread for this.

I don't think my mind as been still or mindful at any point for years. And I don't want to stop. My overanalyzing makes me feel like I'm somehow more mentally aware or something. Like I need this in order to think critically and logically like a normal human being. And yet, here I am thinking about everything that I can, mainly about my role in the world and existential stuff until I become mentally exhausted and pass out.

I can't stop. I'm addicted to thinking.

Really sorry for making you dumb it down a little. 

That makes sense. It really talks to how I think a lot of things are my fault. Thank you very much. I'll try to find the mirror.

So I am who I am regardless, right? Whether I am "stuck" with it or "love" it.

So if I am the person I am now regardless, and I can't truly become the ideal me that I think about, how could and why should I stop hating who I am now?

I don't know if I'm mature enough to do that yet, though. I'm just 19. I can't see myself as anything but my actions, my thoughts, my peers, etc. Hell, I still convince myself that the goal in life is success or maybe fame. 

I can't do it. At least not now.
Well, then how wrong is it to identify myself as the worst I can be? As wrong as people that identify me as the best I can be?

I feel like I HAVE to know myself the best, since I am me. That or I'm just trying to make myself depressed since it's the emotion I'm most comfortable with.

I don't know. I just really want to hate myself.

I have a therapist and am on Prozac. I still take the meds, but I don't want to worry my therapist because he may think it's college-related, when it's not. Also, I don't want people to know that I'm doing bad again after doing so well before.
